copy.title: Making compost
copy.subtitle: The secret’s in the bin
copy.introduction: Composting keeps useful material in the garden. Last year’s plant waste becomes part of next year’s growing medium. The important bit is giving it somewhere convenient to break down.

sections.heading: Compost bin basics
sections.copy: Give your bin a waterproof lid, sturdy sides and a front opening wide enough to work a fork through. A bigger bin holds heat and moisture better. If you buy a plastic bin, check the fit of the lid and hatch.

sections.heading: Why I use three bins
sections.copy: With two bins I used to bag up finished compost to make room for fresh waste. A third bay solved that. When you empty the ready bin, start filling it again. The bins change jobs and the compost stays put.

construction.heading: Building a brick bin
construction.copy: Here’s how I added a third bay beside the original pair. For a timber bin, reclaimed pallet boards work well if you fit them close together. With either material, lay galvanised mesh across the soil to help keep rodents out.

steps.alt: Fresh concrete footing alongside the existing brick bins.
steps.heading: Lay the footing
steps.caption: Pour a level concrete strip under the walls. Leave the centre free of concrete.

steps.alt: New brickwork with a lintel spanning the front opening.
steps.heading: Build the walls
steps.caption: Stagger the brick joints and span the front opening with a lintel.

steps.alt: The new bay with a close-fitting plank door, strap hinges and a hasp.
steps.heading: Fit the door and lid
steps.caption: Hang a close-fitting door. Hinge the lid at the back and cover it with roofing felt.
